html:
On 1 August 1834 Antigua freed all its enslaved people outright, under the Slavery Abolition Act. Most British colonies made freed people serve a further term as apprentices; Antigua's planters chose not to.

The planters knew there was little free land on the island, so freed people would still have to work for wages. The colony's Methodist and Moravian churches had already won many converts among the enslaved.

Freed families founded villages around the island. Their descendants built the trade unions of the 1930s and 1940s that brought Vere Bird to power and led to independence in 1981. Emancipation Day is still marked with the summer Carnival, which recalls the end of colonial slavery.
